name: Chandra
summary: High-angular-resolution X-ray observatory measuring separation between gravitational mass and gas in galaxy clusters, and using spectra to search for decaying dark matter such as sterile neutrinos.
detection_principle: Grazing-incidence mirrors focus X-rays onto imaging / spectroscopic detectors; unidentified narrow lines are sought in galaxy-cluster and galaxy spectra.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: NASA's current mission page lists an “Active Mission”; science-result dates are recorded separately.

collaboration.name: Chandra collaboration / mission team
collaboration.participants_note: Only examples of lead or participating institutions directly established by the sources are listed. This is not a complete collaboration list, and listing does not imply equal institutional roles.

key_parameters.name: Historically disputed spectral line
key_parameters.value: About 3.56 keV; a signal candidate, not established dark matter

results.summary: Reported an unidentified galaxy-cluster line while explicitly requiring further verification of the signal and its origin.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
